Aṇimāṇḍavya
------------------------------------------
A sage by name माण्डव्य was once falsely accused of stealing and was put to death on a spear by the king. But, since he was innocent and had accumulated extraordinary powers by austerities, he did not die. When this was noticed, the king was frightened and got him released. He broke the spear but its ‘aṇi’ or point was firmly imbedded in the sage’s body. Hence he came to be known as अणिमाण्डव्य.
Since he had once killed flies as a child, he was taken to the world of यम after death. But he protested saying that the sin committed by children below four-teen years belongs to their parents. For his mistake of forcing the sage to go to his world, यम was cursed to be born in the human world. He was born as विदुर.

aṇimā
(‘minuteness’)
------------------------------------------
Acquisition of and mastery over super-human powers have always fascinated human beings. The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि, that matchless basic work on the science of योग, calls such powers ‘siddhis.’ Apart from other methods of obtaining such सिद्धिस् as auṣadhi (drugs) or तपस् (austerity), the basic method is to practise the eight steps of योग leading to समाधि (trance). When the pañca-bhūtas (the five elements like earth, water etc.) are chosen as the objects of meditation and समाधि is obtained on them in the prescribed way (vide Yogasūtras 3.44) it leads to the acquisition of the eight supernatural powers called अष्टसिद्धिस् (ibid. 3.45). अणिमा is the first of these सिद्धिस्. As the very name suggests, it is the power to become minute like an ‘aṇu’ or atom in size. हनुमान् is said to have possessed this power.
See also AṢṬASIDDHIS.
